title: Sigil and Salt
premise: August Coldharbour has spent a decade mapping the Thornfell mountains' smuggler roads, staying deliberately invisible to the crown that razed her village. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands, she learns the king is bound to an ancient sigil-entity called the Salt King, which feeds on the realm's grief and will soon consume him entirely—and everyone he rules. Pursued by the king's inquisitor, August gathers a found family of outcasts: a disgraced royal cartographer, a salt-witch exile, and the king's estranged daughter. To unbind the king, they must reach the drowned vault beneath Thornfell where the sigil was first drawn—but doing so requires someone willing to take the binding themselves. In the end, August chooses neither crown nor escape: she redraws the sigil as a shared covenant among the realm's scattered communities, dissolving the Salt King's monopoly on power at the cost of her own invisibility forever.
about_author: Ansel Sandoval is the pen name of a former trail surveyor who spent six years mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who know the land better than the laws that claim it.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Rule
chapters.summary: August Coldharbour's POV. She guides a smuggler caravan through a fog-choked Thornfell pass, demonstrating her encyclopedic knowledge of unmapped roads and her iron rule: never be seen, never be owed. A checkpoint ambush forces her to abandon her maps. Emotional beat: competence masking loneliness; her invisibility is both armor and prison.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: August's POV. At a river ford she finds a dying courier bearing royal seals, who presses a bloodstained map into her hands and whispers 'the crown is not the king.' Inquisitors arrive; she barely escapes. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant responsibility—the map has chosen her whether she likes it or not.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Show
chapters.summary: August's POV, examining the map in a safehouse. It depicts Thornfell but with impossible geography—a drowned vault that appears only when she weeps over it, responding to grief. She realizes it's keyed to sorrow. Emotional beat: uncanny wonder curdling into fear that the map wants something from her.

chapters.title: The Salt-Witch of Greyhollow
chapters.summary: August seeks Maren Voss, a salt-witch exiled for heresy, whose knowledge might decode the sigil. Maren agrees only after testing August's grief with a brutal ritual. Emotional beat: wary mutual recognition between two women who chose exile over complicity.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Hale
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Corwin Hale's POV. He interrogates the ford survivors and deduces the map's bearer is a woman who knows every pass. Flashbacks reveal his genuine belief that order saves lives. Emotional beat: making the antagonist sympathetic—he hunts August not from cruelty but conviction.

chapters.title: The Daughter in Disguise
chapters.summary: August's POV. In a border town she catches a pickpocket who turns out to be Princess Isolde, fleeing a court where her father no longer recognizes her. Isolde confirms the king speaks to his crown at night. Emotional beat: prickly alliance; two women hiding from the same power for different reasons.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: August's POV. The trio travels a smuggler road that shifts unnaturally—the Salt King's influence warping geography itself. Maren teaches them sigil-craft basics. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure, banter against genuine terror.

chapters.title: The Burning of Bellhaven
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. They find a village consumed by white salt-crystal growth, its grieving survivors hollow-eyed and singing to the crown. Isolde confronts what her father's reign feeds on. Emotional beat: horror and guilt; power's cost made visible.

chapters.title: Hale Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Using captured smugglers, he narrows August's likely route and requisitions soldiers, uneasy about orders to burn rather than capture. Emotional beat: first hairline crack in his certainty about justice through law.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: August's POV. Following the map's grief-keyed geography, they descend into a flooded archive beneath Thornfell containing records of the original binding—signed by August's own ancestors. Emotional beat: devastating revelation; her family helped forge the cage now failing.

chapters.title: Blood in the Ink
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The archive reveals the binding requires a Coldharbour's grief freely given. Maren hides this from August while studying countersigils. Emotional beat: protective deception; love expressed as secrecy, planting future betrayal.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Weeping Stair
chapters.summary: August's POV. Hale's soldiers trap them in the archive stairwell. Isolde reveals herself to save them, forcing Hale to choose between duty and regicide-adjacent treason. They escape; Hale lets them go, shaken. Emotional beat: adrenaline and the first fracture in Hale's loyalty.

chapters.title: Audience with the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Captured and brought to court, Isolde faces her father, who briefly surfaces from the Salt King's grip to beg her forgiveness and name the vault's true lock. Emotional beat: heartbreak; a father's love flickering inside his own possession.

chapters.title: The Price Written Down
chapters.summary: August's POV. Maren confesses the binding demands a Coldharbour's willing grief. August rages, then quietly begins copying the original sigil, deciding alone. Emotional beat: betrayal transmuting into grim resolve; she'd always planned to sacrifice herself.

chapters.title: Hale's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Ordered to execute witnesses from Bellhaven, Hale refuses and defects, bringing evidence of the crown's corruption to August's camp. Emotional beat: redemption arc pivot; justice finally diverging from law.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: August's POV. The full company enters the drowned vault through routes only August can navigate, pursued by the Salt King's crystallized dead. Emotional beat: unity forged in extremis; each member's skill indispensable.

chapters.title: The First Binding
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. In the vault's heart they witness the original binding ritual's echo—August's ancestor binding the Salt King to protect a starving realm, a mercy that became a tyranny. Emotional beat: tragic understanding; the villain was once a solution.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: August's POV. The Salt King manifests, offering August power and showing her visions of the realm's suffering if the binding breaks carelessly. It nearly seduces her by validating her rage. Emotional beat: temptation; the corrupting logic of necessary power.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Climax, rotating POVs. August begins the unbinding as Hale holds the passage and Isolde reaches her father. The Salt King fights back through their griefs. August refuses to simply transfer the binding—instead she redraws it as a covenant distributed across all who grieve. Emotional beat: sacrificial courage becoming shared burden.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: August's POV. The vault collapses; the king wakes human and diminished; the Salt King dissolves into ordinary sea-salt. August nearly drowns holding the new covenant-map together and is pulled out by her family. Emotional beat: exhaustion, survival, the cost paid without martyrdom.

chapters.title: A Kingdom of Many Hands
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The aftermath: the king abdicates toward a council including border folk and smuggler enclaves; Hale joins the new order as its conscience. Isolde asks August to map the realm openly. Emotional beat: cautious hope; justice rebuilt outside old law.

chapters.title: The Open Road
chapters.summary: August's POV. Epilogue. August publishes her first map under her own name, then walks into Thornfell with Maren, Hale, and Isolde—not fleeing, but choosing the road. Final image: her ink-stained hands drawing new coastlines. Emotional beat: peace earned; visibility embraced at last.
